properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Idea 12 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 (reflow2 branch feat/vscode-call-door, 2b95bb4, Anthony's work-machine report), with the hook half of idea 1. Opened by triage agent D, 2026-10-02.

THE IDEA, in the report's words: "Ship VS Code hooks: a Stop hook running --call export_graph and a SessionStart hook running --call loop_status. Fixes 4 and 9 without touching the binary. Any shipped command-line guard must parse the executable position, not words in the text (limitation 20)." Idea 1 adds that `reflow2 init --harness vscode-cli` writes them "plus VS Code hook files".

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so this is a HOW question, not a WHETHER:
- dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only (accepted) kept option (b) open: "ship a per-harness equivalent where an event model is confirmed to exist". VS Code's docs now confirm one (fact:vs-code-has-an-agent-hook-event-model-reflow2-can-register-against-2026-10-02).
- dec:idea-a-writing-call-exports-afterwards (settled; step 2 of the door plan) makes a writing call export by itself.
- req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current (step 5) is where any file init writes for this route belongs.

WHY THE EXISTING NUDGE CANNOT SIMPLY BE REGISTERED: loop_nudge.py counts writes by MCP tool name, so a door write is invisible to it. Measured: fact:root-cause-no-loop-nudge-reaches-a-call-door-agent-in-vs-code-2026-10-02.

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) THE REPORT'S MINIMUM. .github/hooks/reflow2.json with SessionStart → `--call loop_status`, its answer returned as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (the docs say it reaches the model), and Stop → `--call export_graph`.
- Cheap: no binary change.
- Counter: Stop → export duplicates step 2 once that lands. On a large design an export per stop costs seconds; a door call on reflow2's own 6,309-node design takes 1–9 s.
(b) PORT THE NUDGE. loop_nudge.py (or a sibling) learns VS Code's payload: count a door write from PostToolUse on the terminal tool, and on Stop block once with {"decision":"block","reason"} (the shape it already prints).
- Counter: counting means reading the command. It must find the executable position and the `--call <tool>` argument, never words in the text (limitation 20; fact:root-cause-a-text-matching-guard-blocks-door-writes-that-mention-remote-shell-words-and-reflow2-ships-no-such-hook-2026-10-02 has an 8-case probe).
- Counter: the terminal tool's name and tool_input shape are not in VS Code's docs.
(c) THE DOOR MARKS ITS OWN WRITES. A writing --call leaves a per-session marker (or loop_status reports writes since the last loop check from the store). The hook then only asks, never parses commands.
- Cleanest against limitation 20.
- Counter: a session id is not passed to --call; "since last check" needs state the core does not keep (fact:root-cause-no-served-read-answers-since-last-time-2026-09-28).
(d) SHIP NOTHING. Fix the stale advisory instead: loop_status should tell a VS Code project a hook is POSSIBLE but not shipped. Keep the instructions file telling the agent to call loop_status.
- Cheapest.
- Counter: rule-by-virtue is what the nudge exists to replace.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS TO SHIPPING ANY HOOK, kept beside it:
- VS Code marks agent-scoped hooks "In Preview", and an organisation can restrict hooks, which the reporter's evidently does for MCP.
- A blocking Stop "consumes AI credits" (VS Code docs).
- Every hook reflow2 ships is another file init/update must keep current (limitation 11).
- Any PreToolUse GUARD is not reflow2's to ship. Limitation 20's guard was the user's or the organisation's, and reflow2 ships none today.

ORDER COST: (a) and (d) can land with step 5. (b) and (c) need the door to stay recognisable in the command text, or a binary change.
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-10-02 — a `--call` agent in VS Code gets the loop through hooks init installs (SessionStart loop_status; Stop export and nudge), with the nudge counting door writes
properties.rationale: Kept open because the settled pieces leave exactly this undecided. The nudge decision allowed a per-harness hook "where an event model is confirmed", and the door plan installs files for VS Code. Neither says which events, which file, or how a hook learns that a door write happened without matching command text. Choosing is Anthony's word.
